task.description:
WF-03 Step 4 DESIGN AMENDMENT for ISS-0119. This is NOT rework of your step-02 handoff -- that handoff's acceptance criteria were met and its gate passed on re-gate pass 3. This is NEW design work responding to a fact that did not exist when you designed: assertion A4 has now been implemented and RUN for the first time, and it found real drift in frozen volume 1 that nobody knew was there. ORCH is dispatching it as its own handoff, at rework_count 0, deliberately -- ORCHESTRATOR.md §5's escalation counter exists to stop a producer looping on the same failed criteria, not to prevent a design responding to new evidence. That reasoning is recorded in the orchestrator log so it can be audited.

THE FINDING. A4 asserts §7's rule: 'every entry carries all five fields in order with a parseable ISO-8601 at:. Exceptions only as declared in A5.' On its first ever run against the fix branch it went RED on three previously undeclared entries in volume 1:
  - line 4803, REQ-053, event started -- NO note: field
  - line 4896, REQ-056, event started -- names its timestamp field `timestamp:` instead of `at:`
  - line 5050, REQ-054, event started -- NO note: field
ORCH independently corroborated this by field-count arithmetic over volume 1 before dispatching you: `- req:`, `event:` and `agent:` each return 183, while `at:` returns 182 and `note:` returns 181 -- one missing `at:` and two missing `note:`, matching the three named lines exactly. This is REAL DRIFT, not a broken test. It is also the single best piece of evidence this whole run has produced: these entries accumulated invisibly for months precisely because no mechanical check existed, and the first mechanical check found them immediately.

WHY TEST-DESIGNER COULD NOT CLOSE IT, and why it was right not to. Remediation lives in docs/status/, which Step 4 was forbidden to touch; and more fundamentally the entries themselves must NEVER be edited -- volume 1 is frozen and pinned by A6, so 'correcting' them is exactly the rewrite the append-only rule forbids. Meanwhile the index has no way to declare a SHAPE violation: `known_anomalies:` is keyed {path,line,field,value} for VOCABULARY violations, and A5 asserts that set equals the on-disk vocabulary-violation set exactly IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, so simply adding the three there would turn A5 red. TEST-DESIGNER explicitly declined to weaken A4 to make the red go away, and said why: a test that only ever runs against already-correct code proves nothing, and suppressing this would be the silent drift ISS-0119 exists to stop. That was the correct call and it is the reason this amendment is needed rather than a quiet edit.

YOUR TASK: amend `lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md` so that A4 can be green on the fix branch WITHOUT weakening what it detects and WITHOUT editing a single byte of frozen volume 1. Two candidate shapes, neither prescribed -- choose on the merits, or propose a third:
  (i) A separate `known_shape_anomalies:` key in the index, keyed to express a MISSING or MISNAMED field (the existing {path,line,field,value} shape may not fit a missing field -- work out the right key), which A4 subtracts from its violation set and which A5 ignores entirely. Parallel to the existing known_anomalies mechanism, and consistent with the design's established honest pattern: never edit, always declare.
  (ii) Scope A4's shape check to the CURRENT volume only, on the argument that a frozen volume's shape is history and cannot be fixed, so asserting over it can only ever produce a permanent red or a permanent exception list. If you choose this, you must say what then prevents the same drift from going undetected in v2 and every future volume, because 'don't check the frozen thing' must not become 'don't check'.
Whichever you choose, THE THREE ENTRIES MUST REMAIN VISIBLE AND DECLARED SOMEWHERE A READER LANDS -- the design's own principle. Silently narrowing A4's scope so the three stop being mentioned anywhere would repeat the failure mode this run exists to fix.

ALSO SPECIFY: the exact index content to be added (ELIXIR-DEV or DOC-UPDATER will apply it), the exact change to A4's and A5's specified behaviour in §7, and any change to §5's anomaly narrative. State explicitly whether your amendment changes the frozen_prefix_sha256 (it must not -- the digest covers volume 1's content, which is not being edited) and whether it changes A5's existing three vocabulary anomalies (it must not).

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: amend only what this finding requires. §8's erratum has already been applied by TEST-DESIGNER under REVIEWER's Step 3d ruling -- do not revisit it. Do not revisit the freeze-and-roll shape, the header text, the 23 instruction sites, or anything else the gate cleared. Do not edit the index, the test files, or volume 1 yourself -- you are designing the amendment, not applying it. Mark the amendment clearly as an amendment, with the date and the finding that prompted it, so a later reader can see the artefact changed after its gate and why.

handoffs/orchestrator.log has uncommitted ORCH edits -- leave it alone, stage by explicit path, never `git add -A`.

=== RE-AMENDMENT ITERATION 1 (dispatched by ORCH 2026-08-21T07:08Z, after CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILed §13 at Step 4e) ===

NINE OF TEN CHECKS PASSED and the gate verified them first-hand rather than from your summary. It wrote its OWN field-set scan of volume 1 and independently reproduced exactly your three entries -- 4803 [event,agent,at], 4896 [event,agent,timestamp,note], 5050 [event,agent,at] -- with no fourth, no extra_field and no field_order case; it parsed §13.4's YAML with a real loader and confirmed it well-formed with all three records matching disk including `found_line: 4899`; it confirmed via `git show --stat 6c999e4` that the change is additive across exactly four hunks with §§1-12 otherwise byte-unchanged; it read the actual vocabulary entries and confirmed A5 disjointness on the data rather than from your argument; and it confirmed check 2's central claim -- bidirectional set equality IS specified in §13.5, not merely prose, so candidate (i) genuinely does not weaken A4. Do not revisit any of that. §§1-12 remain gated and out of bounds.

ONE MAJOR BLOCKS. Check 3 -- 'the exception list cannot grow silently' -- FAILS, and the gate's reasoning is correct. §13.3 gives two grounds. The first (volume 1 is frozen and digest-pinned, so its defect set can never grow) is sound. The second -- that volumes 2 onward are 'checked live while the volume is still current and appendable' -- is exactly the answer the check asks for, AND IT EXISTS ONLY AS PROSE. A4b as specified constrains set equality but places NO CONSTRAINT ON WHICH VOLUME A DECLARED RECORD MAY CITE. So the concrete defeat is: append a malformed entry to the CURRENT volume, add a matching record to `known_shape_anomalies:`, and A4b is green permanently with no gate tripped. The only barriers left are §13.10's instruction and core-directives.md's 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures' -- both addressed to an agent's JUDGEMENT, which is precisely what the Humanless-operation section says a gate must not rest on. This is the declare-to-silence hazard: a mechanism that lets a gate be satisfied by editing what it measures.

THE REQUIRED FIX, which the gate specified precisely: A4b must ADDITIONALLY assert that every `known_shape_anomalies:` record's `path:` names a volume whose index entry has `status: closed` AND carries a `frozen_prefix_sha256:`. No record may cite the current volume. Note what makes this clean -- it changes NONE of your three proposed records, since all three cite volume 1, and it converts §13.3's own second ground from prose into a machine-enforced assertion. That is the whole point: you already made the right argument, it simply was not mechanized. Write it into §13.5 as part of A4b's specified behaviour and update §13.3's prose to cite the assertion rather than assert the property.

MINOR-2, recommended in the same pass, roughly one sentence: A4b's failure-message CONTENT is unspecified, yet §13.9 depends on it -- visibility surface (c) is 'mix test names all three whenever A4b fails'. Specify that A4b's failure output names every element of the symmetric difference, with path, entry_line, req and kind for each, so the claim §13.9 makes is actually guaranteed by the assertion rather than by an implementer's choice.

THREE FINDINGS RECORDED, NOT FOR ACTION THIS PASS -- ORCH's dispositions, so you do not have to decide them:
  - MINOR-2b: A8(c) pins the literal token `known_shape_anomalies:` in the volume header but not the three citations, so a header that keeps the token and drops the citations still passes. Optional strengthening; fold in only if it costs you a clause.
  - MINOR-3: `known_anomalies:`/A5 carries the SAME declare-to-silence hole. OUT OF SCOPE for this run -- ORCH is filing it as its own issue rather than widening a WF-03 fix, and it is flagged here so your parity argument ('the vocabulary mechanism works the same way') is not read as settling it. Do not fix A5 in this pass.
  - The gate's own view on your open question §13.11 #1, which you deliberately left open and were right to: `note:` IS mandatory. Volume 1's own header, in force since before these entries were written, documents the five-field shape with `note:` as the fifth (lines 12-17); v2's header states it in mandatory words; 180 of 182 entries carry it. The fair concession is that v1 PHRASED it as a template rather than as 'required' -- which is exactly what your §13.4 `cause:` field already records. So the exception list is the correct instrument and a weaker A4 is not. You may treat that question as answered and say so.

SCOPE: §13 only, and within it §13.5 plus §13.3's prose, plus MINOR-2's sentence. Nothing else. Append to result.summary as ' || RE-AMENDMENT ITERATION 1 (<timestamp>), addressing CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR Step 4e FAIL (MAJOR-1). ...' and set rework_count to 1.
acceptance_criteria: The amendment is written into lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md and clearly marked as a post-gate amendment with its date and the prompting finding
A mechanism is specified that lets A4 be green on the fix branch without weakening what A4 detects and without editing frozen volume 1
The choice between candidate (i), (ii) or a third option is stated and justified on the merits
The three entries (4803 REQ-053 missing note, 4896 REQ-056 timestamp-instead-of-at, 5050 REQ-054 missing note) remain visible and declared somewhere a reader lands
The exact index content to be added is specified verbatim, ready for ELIXIR-DEV/DOC-UPDATER to apply
The exact changes to A4's and A5's specified behaviour are stated, and A5's existing three vocabulary anomalies are confirmed unchanged
It is stated explicitly that frozen_prefix_sha256 does not change, with the reason
If candidate (ii) is chosen, the artefact states what prevents the same drift going undetected in v2 and future volumes
No file other than the design artefact and this handoff is modified -- the index, the test files and volume 1 are not touched

result.summary:
Design amended: lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md gains section 13, 'POST-GATE AMENDMENT -- 2026-08-21 -- three shape anomalies in frozen volume 1', plus a banner under the title and three cross-reference markers (section 5 preamble, A4, A5). Sections 1-12 are otherwise byte-unchanged; section 8's erratum, the freeze-and-roll shape, the header text and the 23 instruction sites were not revisited.

CHOICE: candidate (i) -- a separate top-level `known_shape_anomalies:` key in docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml, keyed {path, entry_line, req, event, kind, field, found_as, found_line, should_have_been, cause}. A4 splits into A4a (vocabulary, unchanged in substance) and A4b (shape). A4b asserts EXACT SET EQUALITY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS between the shape violations found on disk and `known_shape_anomalies:`, across every volume, closed and current. Candidate (ii) was rejected and the rejection is recorded with reasons in 13.3.

WHY (i) OVER (ii): (i) does not weaken A4 -- it strengthens it. The shape rule still applies to every volume; the three known entries stop being red because they are DECLARED, not because they stopped being checked; and bidirectional equality newly makes a silent 'cleanup' of one of them fail, which A4 could not detect before. The exception list is bounded and permanent by construction (volume 1 is frozen and digest-pinned, so its defect set can never grow), and volumes 2+ are checked live from their first entry, so a defect there is caught while the volume is still appendable. (ii) retires the only enumeration that has ever found these, and defeats itself at roll time: a defect appended late into volume 2 would be checked only until the roll, then silently leave the checked set forever. Its premise -- that asserting over a frozen volume can only yield a permanent red or a permanent exception list -- is factually right but draws the wrong conclusion: a permanent, declared, machine-checked exception list IS the desired outcome, exactly as `known_anomalies:` already is for vocabulary. No third option was needed. One sub-option was considered and rejected: also appending the three to volume 1's closure footer -- legal (the footer sits beyond frozen_prefix_lines: 5766) but it writes bytes into the frozen volume a second time for redundancy the index and the volume-2 header already give.

FINDING CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY before designing, with anchored patterns on the fix branch working tree: '^  - req: ' 182, '^    event: ' 182, '^    agent: ' 182, '^    at: ' 181, '^    note: ' 180, and '^    timestamp: ' matches exactly one line, 4899. One missing `at:` and two missing `note:`, matching the three named entries and nothing else. ORCH's 183/182/181 came from unanchored patterns; the deltas (1 and 2) and the three entries are identical. Real drift, not a broken test.

VISIBILITY (the binding constraint): the three entries are declared in four places a reader lands -- the index's `known_shape_anomalies:` (the file that calls itself THE ENTRY POINT and that every appending agent reads at HOW-TO-APPEND step 1); the current volume's header, via a verbatim addendum specified in 13.8 that names all three by line and req id and says do not copy them and do not clean them up; `mix test`, since A4b names all three whenever it fails in either direction; and this artefact's 13.1 table. A4's scope was not narrowed anywhere.

EXACT CONTENT SPECIFIED FOR SOMEONE ELSE TO APPLY: 13.4 gives the verbatim YAML block to append to the index after the existing `known_anomalies:` block, with all three records and the explanatory comment header. 13.8 gives the verbatim volume-header addendum. 13.5 gives A4a/A4b's exact specified behaviour including the four `kind:` values (missing_field | misnamed_field | extra_field | field_order; only the first two occur), the rule that a misnamed_field is ONE violation not two, the comparison identity key {path, entry_line, kind, field, found_as}, the additional assertion that each record's req/event match what is on disk at entry_line, and the preservation of the ISO-8601 parse for the misnamed timestamp at line 4899. 13.7 gives the two signature-only additions to test/support/status_history.ex (`parse_index/1`'s return map gains `known_shape_anomalies:`; new `shape_anomalies(volume_path)`), and states `anomalies/3` is unchanged.

A5 CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: same text, same behaviour, same three vocabulary anomalies (3490 REQ-031, 3577 REQ-042, 3744 REQ-038, field event, value SCOPE-CHANGE); it must not read `known_shape_anomalies:`. Verified disjoint on the real data -- the three shape-anomalous entries carry req REQ-053/REQ-056/REQ-054 and event `started`, all legal vocabulary, so they never enter A5's on-disk set and A5's verdict is arithmetically unaffected.

frozen_prefix_sha256 DOES NOT CHANGE, stated explicitly in 13.7 with the reason: the digest covers volume 1 lines 1-5766 with CRLF normalised to LF, and this amendment writes zero bytes into docs/status/requirement_status.yaml -- not the prefix, and not the footer beyond it -- so the hashed byte stream is byte-for-byte identical and A6 stays green with no index edit. The digest never covered the index, so adding a key there cannot affect it. A0, A1, A2, A3, A3b, A6, A7 unchanged. A8 gains one clause (c) only: the current volume's header must contain the literal token `known_shape_anomalies:`, so a future volume opened by copy cannot silently drop the declaration at roll time.

Candidate (ii) was not chosen, so the 'what prevents drift in v2 and future volumes' obligation does not bind -- but it is answered anyway by A4b running on every volume forever (13.5) plus A8 clause (c).

Two open questions recorded rather than silently decided (13.11): whether `note:` is genuinely mandatory or only conventional -- deliberately NOT re-decided here, since that is a vocabulary change and not a drift response; and whether `known_anomalies:` should be renamed `known_vocabulary_anomalies:` now that a second class exists.

No implementation code was written -- signatures and YAML/comment content only. Only lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md and this handoff were modified: the index, both test files and volume 1 were not touched, and handoffs/orchestrator.log was left alone (ORCH has uncommitted edits there). Staged by explicit path; no 'git add -A'.

SCHEMA CORRECTION (self-applied after ORCH flagged it): this block first wrote result.status "SUCCESS", which is not a legal value. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2 defines exactly five -- PASS | FAIL | PARTIAL | BLOCKED | SKIPPED (table at :105-111) -- and "PASS" is the correct one here: work complete, acceptance criteria met. Corrected to PASS in a follow-up commit; nothing else in this handoff changed. Recorded rather than silently fixed because Letflow has no handoff linter, so handoff-schema conformance is currently enforced only by an agent noticing -- and HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's own enforcement note cites R-Co measuring 0.4-8.6% compliance for written-down-but-unenforced bookkeeping rules. A next reader should see the correction, not re-derive it. || RE-AMENDMENT ITERATION 1 (2026-08-21T07:11:29Z), addressing CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR Step 4e FAIL (MAJOR-1). The gate passed nine of ten checks and verified them first-hand -- its own field-set scan of volume 1 reproduced my three entries exactly (4803 [event,agent,at], 4896 [event,agent,timestamp,note], 5050 [event,agent,at], no fourth), it parsed 13.4's YAML with a real loader, it confirmed A5 disjointness from the data, and it confirmed via git show --stat 6c999e4 that sections 1-12 were byte-unchanged. None of that was revisited; sections 1-12 remain out of bounds and were not touched again.

MAJOR-1 WAS CORRECT AND IS NOW FIXED. Section 13.3 gave two grounds for the exception list being bounded. The first (volume 1 is frozen and digest-pinned, so its defect set can never grow) was sound. The second (volumes 2 onward are checked live while still appendable) was the right answer but existed ONLY AS PROSE: A4b constrained set equality without constraining WHICH volume a declared record may cite, so appending a malformed entry to the CURRENT volume and declaring it would have left A4b green permanently, with the only remaining barriers -- 13.10's instruction and core-directives.md's 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures' -- addressed to an agent's judgement, which is exactly what Humanless operation says a gate must not rest on. That is the declare-to-silence hazard.

THE FIX, in section 13.5 as part of A4b's specified behaviour: A4b ADDITIONALLY ASSERTS that every known_shape_anomalies: record's path: names a volume whose index `volumes:` entry has `status: closed` AND carries a `frozen_prefix_sha256:`. A record citing the current (open, unpinned) volume, or a path that is not a volume in the index at all, FAILS A4b -- independently of set equality, and even when the on-disk violation it cites genuinely exists. So the only route for a shape defect in the current volume is to fix it in the working tree before committing, which is what 13.3 already said happens. THE THREE RECORDS IN 13.4 ARE UNCHANGED: all three cite docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, closed and digest-pinned, so all three still pass. The same rule is mirrored into 13.4's block comment in the verbatim index YAML (an added comment paragraph: 'A RECORD MAY ONLY CITE A CLOSED, DIGEST-PINNED VOLUME'), so the constraint is stated where the records themselves live and not only in the assertion spec. Section 13.3's bullet was rewritten to CITE that assertion rather than assert the property, and it now says plainly that without the rule the bullet would rest on an agent's judgement.

MINOR-2 FOLDED IN, in 13.5: A4b's failure output is now specified rather than left to the implementer. On any failure -- either direction of set equality, or the closed-volume rule -- the message must name EVERY element of the symmetric difference, one per line, with path, entry_line, req, kind (and field/found_as where set), labelled by side ('on disk but not declared' / 'declared but not on disk'), plus every record that failed the closed-volume rule with the volume status that disqualified it. A count, or 'the sets differ', is explicitly insufficient. That makes 13.9's visibility surface (c) -- mix test names all three whenever A4b fails -- true by specification instead of by an implementer's choice of message.

SECTION 13.11 Q1 ANSWERED ON THE RECORD, per ORCH's disposition: `note:` IS mandatory, not conventional -- volume 1's own header documented the five-field shape with note: as the fifth (lines 12-17) before these entries were written, v2's header states it in mandatory words, and 180 of 182 entries carry it. The fair concession is a wording one -- v1 phrased the shape as a template rather than using the word 'required' -- which is exactly what 13.4's cause: field already records. So the exception list is the correct instrument and a weakened A4b is not. No change to A4b follows.

NOT ACTIONED, per ORCH's dispositions: MINOR-2b (A8(c) pins the token but not the three citations) was left as recorded -- it does not cost 'a clause' to fix properly, since a citation-level assertion needs its own parse of header text against index records, and ORCH marked it optional. MINOR-3 (the same declare-to-silence hole in known_anomalies:/A5) was NOT fixed: ORCH is filing it as its own issue rather than widening a WF-03 fix. Note the consequence for a later reader: after this iteration, shape anomalies are constrained to closed volumes and vocabulary anomalies are not, so 13.3's parity argument ('the vocabulary mechanism works the same way') is now weaker than the shape mechanism, not equal to it -- and that asymmetry is deliberate and temporary, pending MINOR-3's own run.

SCOPE HELD: six hunks, all at line 1077 or later, all inside section 13 -- the iteration-1 marker under 13's Status paragraph, 13.3's bullet, 13.4's comment paragraph, two additions in 13.5, and 13.11 Q1's answer. Sections 1-12 have zero diff. No index, test file or volume-1 byte was touched; frozen_prefix_sha256 still does not change, for the reason 13.7 already gives. handoffs/orchestrator.log was left alone (ORCH has uncommitted edits there); staged by explicit path.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to gate section 13 (it is post-gate design and has not been validated). On PASS, apply in this order: (1) ELIXIR-DEV or DOC-UPDATER appends section 13.4's verbatim block to docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml and inserts section 13.8's verbatim addendum into docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml's header; (2) TEST-DESIGNER implements A4a/A4b per 13.5, the two signature additions to test/support/status_history.ex per 13.7, and A8 clause (c); (3) TEST-RUNNER runs the suite and must report A4b's FULL reported violation set, not just green/red -- if a fourth shape violation appears it is declared in the index with its cause, never suppressed by deleting a record or narrowing the detector (13.10).
